note: Sources: her quantization lecture is the recording transcribed in course/L13.transcript.md (it opens "for this lecture, we will cover large language model quantizations"); course/L12.transcript.md is the serving lecture, and the slide markers in both transcripts point at the other PDF. Slides: course/L12.txt / L12.pdf.
beats: Hook: a handful of giant numbers ruin 8-bit math for everyone else: in a group photo with one friend on stilts, the frame must fit the tallest, and everyone else shrinks to dots (line_outlier_group_photo, line_outlier_print_tiny; full-height vertical option: line_outlier_stilts_tall).

Weights are calm and fixed, so they are measured offline; activations change with every input and carry a few huge channels, the same channels token after token (slide 28; line_outlier_tower_streets).

SmoothQuant (slide 29): Y = (X diag(s)^-1)(diag(s) W): divide each big activation channel by s and multiply the matching weight row by s; the product is unchanged, and both now fit in 8 bits (W8A8) (line_smooth_share_load, line_balance).

LLM.int8() (slide 30): keep the outliers in FP16 and the rest in INT8: accurate, but the separate path is slow on GPUs, sometimes slower than plain FP16 (line_int8_oversize_door); SmoothQuant stays fast at large batches.

KV cache quantization (slide 31): the cloakroom from L03-02 holds activations that stay around; packing it smaller means longer contexts, bigger batches and less traffic per step (line_kv_pack_shrink).

K and V group along different axes (slide 32): one can be packed as each token arrives, the other needs a group of tokens first, so an extra quantization cache waits (line_kv_waiting_trolley). Which is which: check slide 32 (GEMM layout) and M-ANT (Hu et al. 2025; check authors before naming the lab).

NVFP4 (slides 33-34): E2M1 with one scale per block of 16 plus one per tensor, done in Blackwell hardware: a small photo per small group, all pinned on one board; near-original accuracy at 2-3x speed (check) (line_outlier_photo_board).

Vector quantization (slide 35): replace a whole group of numbers with the nearest entry of a small codebook learned by k-means, like printing a picture with a few stamps; mostly for audio and video tokens (line_vq_stamp_set).
Takeaway: the outliers set the scale; split them off (LLM.int8()), move them into the weights (SmoothQuant), or shrink the groups until they cannot hurt (NVFP4).
Cover (line_cover_l12_04; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the group photo: one friend on stilts makes the photographer tilt the camera far back, and everyone else shrinks.

drawings.name: line_outlier_group_photo
drawings.prompt: The photographer (the same character in every picture): an invented adult with a simple round face, dot eyes, a short ponytail, a sleeveless vest with many small pockets over a long-sleeved shirt, working an old wooden box camera on a three-legged wooden tripod. The tall friend (the same character in every picture): an invented cheerful person standing on very tall wooden stilts hidden under extra-long trousers, about three times as tall as everyone else, simple round face, dot eyes, a striped scarf. A group photo outdoors on a lawn. On the right, a row of seven invented friends (simple round faces, dot eyes, different hairstyles: glasses, a ponytail, a cap, curls, a bob, a bun, short spiky hair) stand smiling, and in the middle of them stands the tall friend, whose head nearly reaches the top of the picture, waving. On the left, the photographer has tilted the camera far back on its tripod to fit the tall friend in, and leans back, mouth open, looking up and up. Landscape image 1536x1024; the scene fills about 94% of the width and about 92% of the height. No text, no letters, no numbers, no symbols, no logos anywhere.
